name: Ford-Roman quantum inequality: a bound on the sampled (worldline-averaged) energy density

source.located: arXiv:gr-qc/9607003v2 (24 Jan 1997), L.H. Ford and T.A. Roman, 'Restrictions on Negative Energy Density in Flat Spacetime', TUTP-96-2, dated July 1 1996, revised Oct 2 1996; published Phys. Rev. D 55, 2082 (1997). All 17 pages returned (abstract, Secs. 1-4, Appendices A and B, references).
source.via: alphaXiv answer_pdf_queries(paper='gr-qc/9607003', 7 batched queries) -- page text of the arXiv PDF. Later literature read the same way: gr-qc/9805024 (Fewster-Eveson 1998), 1410.0665 (Kontou-Olum 2015), 2003.01815 (Kontou-Sanders 2020 review); one discover_papers call.

published_statement: Eq. (1) = Eq. (17), verbatim (units hbar = c = 1, metric (-,+,+,+)): rho-hat == (t_0/pi) INT_{-inf}^{inf} <T_00> dt/(t^2 + t_0^2) >= -3/(32 pi^2 t_0^4), 'for all choices of the sampling time, t_0. Here <T_00> is the renormalized expectation value of the energy density evaluated in an arbitrary quantum state |psi>, in the frame of an arbitrary inertial observer whose proper time coordinate is t_0' [sic: t]. p.4: 'the energy density is evaluated in the reference frame of an inertial observer, at an arbitrary spatial point which we choose to be x = 0. The time coordinate t is the proper time of this observer.' Massive 4D scalar, Eq. (16): rho-hat >= -(3/(32 pi^2 t_0^4)) G(2 m t_0), G(0) = 1, G decreasing. Electromagnetic field, Eq. (48): rho-hat >= -3/(16 pi^2 t_0^4). 2D massless scalar, Eq. (25): rho-hat >= -1/(8 pi t_0^2). Sec. 4, verbatim: 'Note that in Minkowski spacetime, our bounds hold for an arbitrary choice of the sampling time, t_0. Recently we argued that such bounds should also hold in a curved spacetime and/or one with boundaries, if the sampling time is restricted to be much smaller than the smallest local radius of curvature and/or the distance to any boundaries in the spacetime [23]. An explicit example of the validity of this assumption has been given in Ref. [24].' Intro p.2-3: 'we recently argued [23] that if one is willing to restrict the choice of sampling time, then the bound should also hold in curved spacetime and/or one with boundaries. For example, we proved that the inequality Eq. (1) holds in the case of the Casimir effect for sampling times much smaller than the distance between the plates.' [23] = Ford & Roman PRD 53, 5496 (1996) = gr-qc/9510071; [24] = Pfenning & Ford gr-qc/9608005.
published_hypotheses: free (uncharged) scalar field, minimally coupled (stress tensor Eq. (6) is the minimal one), mass m >= 0; the massless bound Eq. (17) is the m -> 0 limit of Eq. (16)
four-dimensional Minkowski spacetime, no boundaries ('These inequalities were derived for Minkowski spacetime, in the absence of boundaries')
an arbitrary inertial observer; t is that observer's proper time; the density is evaluated at ONE spatial point x = 0 on the worldline
sampling function t_0/[pi (t^2 + t_0^2)] (Lorentzian), unit integral, width t_0; the bound holds for every t_0 > 0

'an arbitrary quantum state |psi>' -- with the derivation's implicit conditions: expectation values of a^+ a and a a exist, the mode sums converge ('So long as the resulting sums are convergent, which is the case for the systems with which we are concerned', App. B), quantisation in a finite box V with discrete frequencies and lowest frequency > 0 before V -> infinity
<T_00> is the renormalised (normal-ordered against the Minkowski vacuum) energy density
no optimality is claimed for the 4D constant; for 2D massive the paper says the bound 'is not optimal over this range' (y in [0, 1.2])

Sec. 4 curved/boundary extension: NOT a hypothesis of Eq. (1) -- an 'argued' extrapolation from [23], conditional on sampling time << smallest local radius of curvature and << distance to any boundary; the paper calls it 'this assumption' and cites one proved boundary case (Casimir plates) and one worked example (static Robertson-Walker, [24])

It maps onto Kontou-Olum 2015's explicit criterion R_max t_0^2 << 1 (G_00 is a Ricci component, so R_max t_0^2 >= (b/l_G)^2 = 3750 on the corridor): the tree's H2 verdict is corroborated by the later theorem, not weakened.

QUOTATION SPLICE (discrepancy, not refutation): achievable.py:227-231 quotes 'we recently argued that such bounds should also hold in a curved spacetime and/or one with boundaries, IF the sampling time is restricted to be much smaller than the smallest local radius of curvature.' The Sec. 4 sentence reads 'Recently we argued that ... the smallest local radius of curvature and/or the distance to any boundaries in the spacetime [23]'; 'we recently argued' is the Introduction's wording (p.2). Substance faithful; the 'argued' reading is the paper's own word, and Sec. 4 calls it 'this assumption'.

ATTRIBUTION (discrepancy): achievable.py:120-121 'Ford & Roman's own practice of sampling at a hundredth of the geometric scale' -- no such practice appears in gr-qc/9607003; it belongs to the wormhole/warp applications ([23], Pfenning-Ford gr-qc/9702026), NAMED-NOT-READ here. index3.py:1224 calls the flat bound 'Pfenning-Ford's 1997 result'; it is Ford-Roman's (originally PRD 51, 4277 (1995), re-derived here). Neither moves a figure.

SCOPE (correct, worth stating): certify.py:154-159 'Ford-Roman bounds a SAMPLED energy density along a worldline ... no standard QI bounds [the ball integral] directly' matches the paper's p.4 statement and is confirmed by Ford-Helfer-Roman gr-qc/0208045 (read by the tree in D55): no purely spatial QI exists in 4D.

rederivation.outcome: ALL CHECKS PASS (31 checks; ~3 min, most of it z3). sympy: the Lorentzian transform (8)->(9) gives e^{-d t_0}; the prefactor chain (12)->(13) is 1/(4 pi^2); INT w^3 e^{-2 w t_0} gives exactly -3/(32 pi^2 t_0^4) (17); G(0) = 1 and G strictly decreasing (no 4D peak, as the paper says); EM (48) = -3/(16 pi^2 t_0^4) = exactly 2 x scalar; 2D (25) = -1/(8 pi t_0^2); the Bessel form (20)-(23) checked numerically, F(0+) = 1, and the paper's 2D 'small peak' on 0 <= y <= 1.2 is real (max F = 1.0616). z3 (nlsat): Appendix B's lemma S_m >= S~_m, encoded with A_i = e^{2 w_i t_0} - 1, 0 <= A_1 <= ... <= A_n (all the proof uses), is UNSAT-on-negation at n = 2 (full PSD C via minors) and n = 3, 4 (rank-one C, which suffices because the claim is linear in C); the induction (B17)-(B21) is verified as a polynomial identity at n = 4 in sympy; 200 random Hermitian PSD draws at n = 8 agree. SI form: achievable.ford_roman_allow matches 3 hbar/(32 pi^2 c^3 t_0^4); the 105.276 fixture is 32 pi^2/3. Later literature checked against the paper: Fewster-Eveson (5.6) = 27/(2048 pi^2 t_0^4) = 9/64 of Ford-Roman (fewsterteo.NINE_64 independently reproduced); Flanagan's 2D optimal bound on the Lorentzian is FR/6 and Fewster-Eveson's 2D is FR/4, as they state; Kontou-Olum's Gaussian leading term 3.76 = 3 sqrt(pi/2). Kontou-Olum's smallness criterion R_max t_0^2 << 1 evaluated on the corridor: >= 3750 (noise.B_OVER_LG_SQUARED), so H2's failure is the later theorem's own verdict.

later_literature.what: General worldline QI for any smooth even non-negative sampler of rapid decrease, all d >= 2, m >= 0: rho_f >= -(1/16 pi^2) INT (sqrt f)''^2 in 4D massless (5.5). On the Lorentzian: -27/(2048 pi^2 t_0^4), '9/64 of Ford and Roman's result' -- Ford-Roman's constant is valid but not optimal (NARROWS the constant, tightening every refusal). Compact-support samplers remove 'any remaining doubt that the quantum inequalities of Ford and Roman might rely on subtle large scale effects'. Massive 4D: the massless bound is also a lower bound (Q_3 in [0,1]). States: 'sufficiently well-behaved'; rigorous class expected to be Hadamard.

Optimal 2D massless bound -(1/24 pi) INT f'^2/f: six times stronger than Ford-Roman's 2D Lorentzian bound (re-derived here from Fewster-Eveson's restatement). Bears on Eq. (25), not on the 4D Eq. (1) the tree uses.

No purely spatially averaged QI over bounded regions exists in 4D Minkowski, over Hadamard states satisfying the temporal inequality. Fixes the reach of Eq. (1) to worldline averages -- exactly the scope certify.py:154-159 and bounds.py F2/F3 assign it.

later_literature.what: Proves the Sec. 4 extrapolation to first order in the Ricci tensor and its derivatives for the massless minimally coupled scalar on a timelike geodesic: bound = flat Fewster-Eveson term + corrections of order R_max t_0^2, R''_max t_0^4, R'''_max t_0^5 (Eqs. (128), (130)); 'Ford and Roman [6] have argued that flat-space quantum inequalities can be applied in curved spacetime ... The present paper explicitly confirms this claim and calculates the magnitude of the deviation.' Caveats that SHARPEN Ford-Roman's condition: curvature must be small over the whole causal region between path points, the scale of curvature VARIATION must also exceed t_0, an ambiguity from the renormalisation constants a, b remains, and no first-order correction on Ricci-flat paths (second-order terms exist). One wording discrepancy in their conclusion ('radius of curvature is small as compared to the sampling time' -- inverted; their Sec. VIII states it the right way round) -- a misprint, not quoted as an error.

Review, Eq. (61)-(63): the 4D worldline QWEI holds for all Hadamard states; 'for a Lorentzian function, C = 3/(32 pi^2)'; first derived by Ford and Roman [73, 74]. Table 3: state-independent QEIs exist for massless/massive minimally coupled Klein-Gordon, Maxwell/Proca, Dirac, 2D CFT, Ising; impossible for non-minimally coupled Klein-Gordon (state-dependent ones exist); null-line QEIs do not exist in 4D (Fewster-Roman 2003).

No state-independent QEI for the non-minimally coupled scalar (an N-particle tensoring argument); non-trivial state-dependent bounds exist. Limits Eq. (1)'s field hypothesis H1 -- the tree records this at achievable.py caveat (a) and overturn L4 (candidate D).

later_literature.ref: Pfenning, PRD 65, 024009 (2002); Fewster & Pfenning, J. Math. Phys. 44, 4480 (2003), gr-qc/0303106
later_literature.what: State-independent QWEIs for the electromagnetic and Proca fields on globally hyperbolic spacetimes -- the rigorous successor of the paper's Sec. 3 (Eq. (48)).

Null-geodesic QEIs do not exist in 4D Minkowski (explicit counter-example); Freivogel & Krommydas 2018 argue a cutoff-dependent smeared null bound survives (contested). Bears on the null cousins, not on Eq. (1).
State-independent QEI in an interacting model (massive Ising, 2D); the general interacting 4D case remains open (2003.01815 Sec. 3.2).

lacked_data: M's hypothesis has no purchase on this result, and the evidence is the derivation itself: Eq. (1) contains no empirical input. Its inputs are the canonical commutation relations, the positivity of a norm (Appendix A: <O^+ O> >= 0), an ordering lemma on exponentials (Appendix B), and one Gamma-function integral; hbar and c enter only as units (moving hbar from CODATA 1986 to the 2019 exact value shifts any figure by 3.5e-7 orders). What came LATER was mathematics, not data, and every piece of it TIGHTENED or CONFIRMED the bound: Fewster-Eveson 1998 lowered the Lorentzian constant to 9/64 of Ford-Roman's and freed the sampler; Fewster 2000 and the review fix the state class at Hadamard; Ford-Helfer-Roman 2002 showed the worldline restriction is essential (no spatial version); Kontou-Olum 2015 proved the Sec. 4 extrapolation to first order with its condition sharpened. The only place a later FINDING loosens things is on the field-content hypothesis H1: Fewster-Osterbrink 2008 showed non-minimally coupled scalars admit no state-independent QEI, and interacting 4D theories have none proved (review Table 3). That is a hypothesis about which fields exist, not a datum the authors lacked; the tree already carries it (achievable.py caveat (a), overturn L4). No experiment has refuted a QI; squeezed light (Wu et al. 1986, cited by the paper) and the Casimir density (3-7 % of the bound, Fewster 1208.5399) sit inside it. Evidence against M's hypothesis here: the result's grade did not move in thirty years of successors, and its one non-optimality was in M's disfavour (the bound got tighter).
grade_evidence: Eq. (1) STANDS: the statement and hypotheses as the load-bearing owners use it (achievable.ford_roman_allow, bounds.py Z = 1, ledger W1, noise.py H2, fewsterteo NINE_64, certify.py QI_BOUNDS) match the paper READ at source -- a Lorentzian TIME average at ONE point, free minimally coupled scalar, 4D Minkowski, every t_0, arbitrary (rigorously: Hadamard) state. The re-derivation agrees with the source at every closed-form step (sympy), Appendix B's lemma is machine-checked (z3, n = 2, 3, 4) and the bound has been re-proved and tightened by successors (Fewster-Eveson 9/64, verified). No datum enters, so no moved datum can move it. The three owners that still print the withdrawn spatial-scale form (candidates.py, overturn.py, spec.py) drop the theorem's hypotheses; that is the tree's own W1 withdrawal and specthm's STALE-TEXT record, not a fault of the result, and this grade does NOT extend to those sentences. Sec. 4, graded separately as the split note asks: an EXTRAPOLATION the paper itself calls 'argued' and 'this assumption'; it is now a THEOREM to first order in curvature (Kontou-Olum 2015, READ) under a condition SHARPER than the paper's -- curvature and its variation small over the causal region, R_max t_0^2 << 1 -- so as a claim it STANDS in its stated regime and is NARROWED in the sense that the condition has more clauses; the tree uses it only as the condition H2 is measured against and finds the corridor OUTSIDE it (R_max t_0^2 >= 3750), which Kontou-Olum's criterion confirms. Nothing here is a refutation of anything the tree relies on.
what_would_change_the_grade: WRONG would need a Hadamard state of the free massless minimally coupled field in 4D Minkowski whose Lorentzian time-average at one point falls below -3/(32 pi^2 t_0^4) -- and since Fewster-Eveson prove the tighter -27/(2048 pi^2 t_0^4) on the same class, such a state would refute both; none is known. NARROWED for the theorem would need the rigorous state class to be smaller than Hadamard (no such result is known; Fewster-Eveson expected 'conceivably for all Hadamard states' and the review states it for all Hadamard states). For Sec. 4: a second-order computation showing the curvature corrections are NOT small when R_max t_0^2 << 1 and the variation scale exceeds t_0 would narrow the extrapolation; a proof at all orders would remove 'argued' entirely. DATA-DEPENDENT is unreachable: no measured quantity enters. For the tree (not the grade): repairing candidates.py/overturn.py/spec.py's stale spatial-scale text under W1 would leave nothing in the tree using the result outside its hypotheses.
